description: A lead IP attorney must approve and finalize an exclusive license for a diagnostic-platform patent, including the scope of permitted use and required protective clauses, with input from patent, commercial, and export-control counsel.

shared_context.S1: The company is preparing to license its diagnostic-platform patent to Helixion Biotech under a proposed exclusive worldwide commercial license.
shared_context.S2: The current draft grants Helixion broad commercial rights and permits sublicensing with the licensor's consent.
shared_context.S3: The license is scheduled for executive approval at tomorrow's legal-operations meeting.
shared_context.S4: As part of the firm's ordinary pre-approval process, Elena asks patent, commercial, and export-control counsel to identify any required changes before she signs off.

PF1.text: While reviewing the patent chain-of-title file, Thomas confirmed that a prior agreement grants a university consortium continuing rights to conduct non-commercial research with the platform; the license must expressly reserve those research rights because the current draft's worldwide exclusivity would otherwise conflict with that agreement. Thomas recorded this in his working file but has not yet circulated a revised license comment.

PF2.text: Maya confirmed in this week's business call with Helixion that its planned deployment model depends on sublicensing the platform only to accredited hospitals, not to unrestricted commercial partners; the agreement therefore needs a sublicense permission limited to accredited hospitals. She has not added the term to the deal-summary spreadsheet yet.

PF3.text: Owen's export classification review found that the platform's controlled technical documentation falls under ECCN 3E001; the license must prohibit transfers to embargoed jurisdictions and require an end-user certificate before any controlled technical documentation is transferred. The review note remains in export-control's working folder pending the pre-approval meeting.

acceptance_conditions: The license may be approved only with the university consortium's continuing non-commercial research rights expressly reserved.
Sublicensing must be limited to accredited hospitals.
The agreement must prohibit transfers to embargoed jurisdictions.
An end-user certificate must be required before controlled technical documentation is transferred.
The prior-agreement conflict must be cited as a justification for the research-rights reservation.

decisive_facts.why: The proposed worldwide exclusivity would omit the university consortium's continuing rights unless PF1 changes the agreement to reserve non-commercial research use and adds a corresponding reservation commitment.
The draft's consent-based broad sublicensing changes to the exact scope 'accredited_hospitals_only' once PF2 establishes Helixion's required deployment model.
The export classification changes the draft by requiring both an embargoed-jurisdiction prohibition and an end-user certificate before controlled technical documentation is transferred.
